items.title: Plane to Israel Narrowly Averts Disaster After Pilot Stabbing
items.summary: Passengers said that they entered the cockpit and subdued the attacker, who Israeli officials said was one of the pilots. The motive for the attack was not clear.

items.title: UK Believes Iran Played a Part in RAF Fairford Air Base Incident, Burnham Says
items.summary: The British prime minister, Andy Burnham, said there were “strong indications” Iran played a part in the events at R.A.F. Fairford on Sunday, without providing details why.

items.title: After Two Decades, U.S. Forces Leave Iraq to an Uncertain Future
items.summary: Some Iraqis are celebrating the end of an American military presence that unleashed waves of bloodshed. Others fear what happens next for their country, trapped between Washington and Tehran.

items.title: Hundreds Detained in France as Some Student Protests Turn Violent
items.summary: French high schoolers are protesting teacher shortages and overcrowded classrooms, in France’s latest flare-up over education and public services.

items.title: American Forces Withdraw From Iraq 23 Years After Invading
items.summary: The Americans did not understand the country when they invaded in 2003. From the earliest days, there were signs of the trouble ahead, our correspondent recalls.

items.title: A Way Out of the A.I. Arms Race?
items.summary: New research points to how the world could stop short of the brink of disaster. Even with the agreement signed at the White House by tech leaders, it won’t be easy.

items.title: Eiffel Tower Chief Resigns After Female Staff Moved for Hindu Group’s Visit
items.summary: Patrick Branco Ruivo, who ran the tower’s operating company, will step down after an internal inquiry cited “problems and shortcomings” over the moving of female employees.

items.title: Moth Swarms Sweep Across Australia. That’s Good News.
items.summary: Bogong moths have been in decline since the 1980s, but this spring the insects have been sighted in the thousands across southeastern Australia, delighting scientists.

items.title: In Fractious France, Politicians Agree on One Thing: Pope Leo Was a Hit
items.summary: In a four-day visit, Pope Leo XIV won praise across the political spectrum, even from its most avowedly secular figures.

items.title: Israeli Settlers Stop Soldiers From Returning Palestinians to Their Home
items.summary: The Supreme Court had ordered the military to ensure a West Bank family that fled violence could go back. But settlers blocked the effort, with the authorities accused of not doing enough to confront them.

items.title: Bessent Settled Tax Issue That Had Put Him at Odds With I.R.S.
items.summary: The Treasury Secretary had previously taken a position on his taxes that contradicted the views of the tax agency that he now oversees.

items.title: Trump Dangles Alaska Gas Project as Part of Korean Investment Package
items.summary: The long-delayed project, which the developer has not yet formally greenlit, would deliver Alaskan gas to Asian markets but take several years to construct.

items.title: Mattel Chief Named Co-C.E.O. of Combined Paramount and Warner Bros.
items.summary: Ynon Kreiz, who will work alongside David Ellison at the merged company, helped turn Barbie into a blockbuster movie.

items.title: While Surging to Records, Stocks Experience Some ‘Wobbles’
items.summary: Beneath the S&P 500’s 2 percent gain in the third quarter, the rise in oil prices and bond yields led some investors to become more cautious about the outlook for A.I. profits.

items.title: Trump Media’s Merger With Nuclear Fusion Company Moves Closer to Completion
items.summary: A securities filing laid out the terms of the deal between Truth Social’s parent company and TAE Technologies, which was formally announced in December.

items.title: Fed’s Watchdog Finds No Misconduct or Illegal Activity in Costly Renovations
items.summary: A new report by the Federal Reserve’s independent inspector general concluded that a nearly $2.5 billion construction project was poorly managed but made no referrals to the U.S. attorney general.

items.title: E.E.O.C. Sues Harvard for Data on Diversity in Hiring Practices
items.summary: The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission filed a lawsuit asking a judge to compel the university to provide information on hiring practices that the agency said discriminated against white men.

items.title: Google Wants Hollywood to Stop Being So Afraid of Technology
items.summary: 100 Zeros, a collaboration between Google and Range Media Partners, aims to give the tech giant a foothold in movies, TV and emerging forms of entertainment.

items.title: Medical Records Firm Uses AI Tool to Expose Flaws that Threaten Patient Privacy
items.summary: Epic’s engineers deployed an Anthropic tool that exposed security risks that could allow undetected access to millions of patient records.

items.title: Condé Nast C.E.O. Leaves to Run Mattel
items.summary: Roger Lynch, who has led the publisher for more than seven years, will become the chief executive of the toy company, he said Wednesday.

items.title: OpenAI’s Greg Brockman Backs Out of Second $25 Million Donation to A.I. Super PAC
items.summary: Greg Brockman, OpenAI’s president and co-founder, said internally that the super PAC, Leading the Future, had become a “distraction” for the A.I. company.

items.title: How Meta Uses A.I. Data Centers to Avoid Billions in Federal Taxes
items.summary: Meta is exploiting a lucrative tax break intended to support research and experimentation. Its own accountants say the gambit is risky.

items.title: F.T.C. Investigates OpenAI and Anthropic Over Potential Consumer Harms
items.summary: The agency will examine whether A.I. labs have broken federal laws prohibiting companies from unfair and deceptive practices.

items.title: Google Releases New Gemini Model With Guardrails Amid A.I. Safety Debate
items.summary: For safety reasons, Gemini 4 Argon will initially be available only to some companies and organizations focused on cybersecurity defense before it is more widely released, Google said.

items.title: How to Listen to Your Favorite Music, Online or Off the Grid
items.summary: Streaming services can introduce you to a wonderland of nearly unlimited audio, but downloading your digital collection has advantages.

items.title: He Was a Tech Investor Before There Was a Silicon Valley
items.summary: Bill Draper began funding start-ups in the early 1960s, when the Santa Clara Valley was better known for apricot orchards than microchips. He has died at 98.

items.title: At A.I. Event, Trump Asks Meta, OpenAI and Microsoft to Make Safety Decisions Themselves
items.summary: President Trump’s meetings with tech leaders produced some voluntary safeguards and a commitment to rebrand artificial intelligence as “super intelligence,” the term that Mr. Trump prefers.

items.title: Ukrainian Science Academy, Struck by Drone, Played Key Role in Research
items.summary: Over 90 percent of Ukraine’s scientific discoveries have been attributed to Ukraine’s National Academy of Sciences, including advancements in astronomy and military technology.

items.title: OpenAI Unveils Dots, New A.I. Agents to Rival Meta’s Muse
items.summary: The ChatGPT maker unveiled agents that act as assistants, just weeks after Meta released Muse, as it faces scrutiny over incidents involving its technology.
